Punnett square: gametes of Ff = F, f; gametes of ff = f, f →
      |  F  |  f
  f   | Ff  | ff
  f   | Ff  | ff
Offspring: 2 Ff (free) : 2 ff (attached) = 1 : 1 (50% free, 50% attached). Parents' genotypes: Ff and ff.
explanation_steps: Attached-lobed offspring (ff) must receive an f allele from EACH parent, so both parents carry f.
If both parents were Ff the ratio would be 3 free : 1 attached; if one parent were FF all offspring would be free.
Only Ff × ff gives 1 free : 1 attached – this is a test-cross ratio.
Draw the Punnett square to show 2 Ff : 2 ff.

similar_questions.answer: Mendel's Law of Dominance states that in a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic. Rather than both alleles contributing to a phenotype, the dominant allele will be expressed exclusively.

similar_questions.stem:
Write two activities that occur during the interphase of cell cycle.
9.1 ____________________
9.2 ____________________
similar_questions.answer:
9.1 DNA replication (synthesis of a new set of DNA).
9.2 Growth of the cell and duplication of organelles.
explanation_steps:
**Interphase** is the longest part of the cell cycle. During this phase: 
1. The cell grows in size (G1 phase). 
2. **DNA replication** occurs (S phase) to ensure both daughter cells get a copy. 
3. Mitochondria and other organelles duplicate (G2 phase).
